A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OMA benchmark and MAT framework despite changes in title and terminology. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original OMA/OMA-GT evaluations, component ablations, model-size comparisons and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original MAT evaluations and reports additional baseline comparisons, geographic transfer, data-efficiency, corruption and geometric-complexity results.

M1.justification: The vector encoder, PA/SA attention, association head, CE+CTC objective and beam decoding largely match. However, v1 explicitly applies multidimensional RoPE in both attention modules; v3 removes its description and ablation without clarifying whether RoPE was removed from the model or only from the documentation.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluations using MapTR and SeqGrowGraph predictions, nuScenes-C rain/fog/darkness conditions, corrupted SD maps and an occlusion case study. These expand the evaluated input conditions substantially. The original nuScenes/OSM cities and sample counts remain; renaming OMA-GT as OMA Train/Val does not establish additional coverage.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained KNN and HMM comparisons, v3 Tables 1–2 evaluate DeepMM, MTrajRec, GraphMM, EAM3, GMT and FastMAC. Table 3 also adds an evaluated PTv3 baseline. These substantially broaden the comparator set beyond v1.

E3.justification: v3 introduces cross-city training/testing, 1–100% training-data subsets, clean-trained zero-shot corruption evaluation and complexity-stratified scoring. Reported training settings also change: v1 Appendix F.2 gives learning rate 2e-3 and batch size 12, whereas v3 Appendix I.2 gives 1e-4 and 128. These are reporting revisions, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds geographic-transfer and data-efficiency studies, complexity-dependent error analysis, SD-map and weather robustness tests, and occlusion analysis. Tables 13–19 add sensitivity studies of crop size, spatial discretization, loss weights, serialization curves, beam width and metric settings. Existing attention visualizations persist, while the RoPE-specific ablation disappears.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, actual experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v3 promises future release of random seeds but supplies no experiment-specific seed or uncertainty information. Its new metric stratification does not provide uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Numerous baseline, transfer, corruption and sensitivity results are added. The MapTRv2-test MAT-L entry changes from 42.3 in v1 Table 1 to 45.0 in v3 Table 2; revised training documentation prevents treating this as an established same-setting gain. The clean-map score remains 78.7, with v3 explicitly labeling validation precision as NR-F1. Threshold-specific scores and MAT-S/M result rows are removed.

T1.justification: v3 adds a Fréchet-distance-based complexity measure and equally weighted bin-scoring definition, plus computational-complexity assertions for PA and SA in Appendices E.2 and F. Core graph definitions, association mathematics, metric pseudocode and beam-search equations largely persist. No new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: OMA, the navigation-oriented metric and MAT remain the core contributions. v3 broadens the headline performance claim to superiority over learned matching methods and emphasizes real-time GIS/navigation applications under the ONR framing. Its highlighted 34 ms MAT-T result already appeared in v1’s appendix, so this does not establish a new speed contribution.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations of geographic and generator transfer, annotation efficiency, corruption tolerance and aggregate-score bias toward simple roads. It identifies geometric complexity as an important failure boundary. It also replaces v1’s explanation of poor CTC-only performance with low-sensitivity language despite retaining the 67.7 versus 78.7 gap, and changes the stated future-work limitations.

D1.justification: v3 adds transition-boundary annotation rules, beam width 4 and expanded release/maintenance plans, while resolving several conflicting training specifications. It no longer discloses v1’s proprietary-Chinese-map MAT preannotation stage or the unoptimized CPU-baseline timing caveat; this does not establish that annotation was redone. Weight decay still conflicts between main text and appendix, and release statements mix present availability with future promises.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially recast around learned map matching, graph/point matching and SD-prior mapping, including SMERF, P-MapNet and TopoSD. Appendix C expands positioning relative to end-to-end planning and NavigScene. Conversely, v1’s explicit PTv3 methodological attribution and RoPE-related citations disappear.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, attention explanations and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Terminology systematically shifts from online HD maps and Association P-R to OP maps and NR P-R. The appendices are reorganized with a contents list, dataset Q&A and separate analysis sections, and the repeated bibliography is removed.

P2.justification: v3 redraws the navigation and metric illustrations, restructures comparison tables with method-category and generator columns, and splits the combined ablation table. It adds complexity plots and corruption/generator visualizations. Earlier attention, association and failure-case figures are largely retained but relocated within a substantially revised layout.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses v1’s narrow empirical support: KNN/HMM comparisons under one predicted-map generator are expanded to learned baselines, multiple generators, geographic transfer and controlled corruptions. The complexity analysis also exposes an important failure boundary. These materially strengthen assessment of MAT’s usefulness. Reporting weaknesses temper the gain: RoPE and annotation provenance become unclear, weight-decay settings remain inconsistent, and Tables 9–10 disagree with the stated bin-averaging rule. Nevertheless, the broader comparative evidence and failure characterization constitute a substantial overall improvement.
